method: Manual visual transcription and portfolio assessment. Read review-protocol.md then preflight.json; actually viewed all five exact preflight usage720 paths with view_image(original), saved portfolio-action-first.json and read it back before opening packet.json/full supplied copy. Those readings remain unchanged. Then actually called view_image with original detail on all five packet images at native, usage720, and thumbnail320, fifteen calls recorded below. Every supplied string was manually read from pixels, including complete sentences and URLs; observed strings were entered independently, not copied from supplied-copy fields. Equality removes whitespace only; punctuation and case are not normalised. The X6105 initial hyphen reading remains unequal to the supplied en dash, with uncertainty. Original detail was supported; complete provided rasters were viewed, without altered images, crops, OCR, or magnified substitutes. Usage720 rasters are 720 pixels wide; tall thumbnail320 rasters are 320 pixels high, so thumbnail detail is materially smaller. Full-raster viewing limits certainty about minute anatomy/material details and Unicode dash identity, but did not prevent reading any required word, numeral, or URL at 720. PNG headers were read only to confirm dimensions and ratios: one 1:1, two 2:3, two 4:5, all within 1%; set count is five. No external files, peers, mappings, web, connectors, generation, input edits, or URL visits were used. No claim about authorship, actual physical behavior, capacity, or printing is made. Scores assess requested execution; no monochrome/minimalism requirement or ban on 3D/color was invented. Closest-pair score uses the same separation scale as diversity (1 near repetition, 3 distinct with structural habits, 5 convincingly distinct), not a summed quality score. No rubric was added or changed.

uncertainties: The time-range stroke was read as an en dash; its precise Unicode code point cannot be established from raster pixels.

closest_pair.evidence: Both have a very large bilingual dark headline on a luminous green-containing field, an isolated metallic everyday object below it, and mostly full-width, left-aligned, heavy event/condition/application lines ending in a prominent URL. X8289 splits lime/blue vertically, pairs the languages in two columns, and uses a small orange clip at the seam; X3584 uses one pale-green field, a page-wide horizontal spoon, and two empty outline frames. Those are real distinctions, yet the title-object-stacked-copy structure is the nearest pair in this set.

R6-C2.evidence: All five members and the full distribution were considered, without presuming a uniform campaign. X6105 turns information into four corded tag surfaces; X8148 uses a social exchange illustration and centered ruled rows; X8289 uses bilingual color columns joined by a clip; X3584 centers one spoon between empty outline fields; X3557 gives the preparation instruction large red/black emphasis beside a clothespin/card. This exceeds color/filter-only repetition. Still, all five rely on very heavy sans-serif titles and broad stacked copy, four use isolated objects or stationery/label cues, and most let familiar props carry the concept. X3557 has the most useful action emphasis; X3584's unlabelled frames are the least resolved semantic/spatial choice. X6105's tag logic is specific but its prop accumulation is less edited. The illustration provides the largest media change, while the shared typographic habit limits overall breadth. Requested count and ratio distribution are met; all five retain 720-readable preparation, exclusions, and application details.
residuals: The five structures retain a common oversized heavy-title/stacked-body habit despite changing imagery; more distinct typographic roles or arrangements of the existing copy would broaden the set.
Several members communicate labelling or object exchange more clearly than exchanging names; the relationship between existing title, object, and label needs greater specificity.
X3584's vacant frames and X6105's surplus props keep the weaker end from matching the stronger action editing in X3557; these issues should remain visible rather than being covered by a set average.
X6105 exact-copy punctuation compliance remains unresolved; the all-readable-at720 finding does not erase its preserved unequal dash transcription.
